title: Muffin — Node & services
description: The single Always-Free node: 24 GB, 4 OCPU, arm64. OCI Monitoring covers the VM but cannot see inside a container, and per-container memory is exactly what bites here.

panels.title: Memory used, as a share of each container's OWN limit
panels.description: THE PANEL THAT MATTERS. '1.4 GB' means nothing until you know the ceiling is 1.5 GB and not 4 GB. openbb-api was OOM-killed at its 1 GB limit by ONE exploratory request — `Exited (137)`, ~15s of every market tool down, host memory fine throughout. From `docker stats` via node-exporter's textfile collector, once a minute: cAdvisor cannot identify a container on this node (containerd image store — see the stack file).

panels.title: Host memory
panels.description: Measured 2026-08-27: 7,913 MB used of 23,974, i.e. 16 GB available — against ~21.9 GB of declared limits across 32 services, because usage runs far under the ceilings.

panels.title: Filesystem used
panels.description: `/` was at 70% on 2026-08-27 and GROWS WITH EVERY IMAGE PULL: Docker uses the containerd image store, so images live in /var/lib/containerd (20 G) rather than the migrated data-root on /mnt/data (9% of 98 G). daemon.json's `data-root` does not control that. See todos.md.

panels.title: CPU by service
panels.description: Percent of ONE core; the node has 4.

panels.title: Public requests by router
panels.description: Everything a visitor actually hit — the app, the chat UI, the API, Supabase and Studio. The only place the request path is measured end to end.

panels.title: Disk — where the space actually goes
Disk by docker volume
panels.description:
Every named docker volume, stacked. This is the panel to read when a filesystem chart moves and you want to know WHY. Measured 2026-08-28: muffin_supabase-db-data 8.4 GB, http-cache 0.6, firecrawl-postgres 0.1, prometheus 0.05, grafana 0.05 — so /mnt/data is essentially the Postgres volume, and its sawtooth is WAL recycling and vacuum.

Anonymous volumes are deliberately excluded: their names are 64-hex ids that tell a reader nothing and change on every redeploy, so including them would grow series cardinality without bound.

panels.title: Image store and superseded directories
panels.description:
`/var/lib/containerd` is the IMAGE STORE and it is NOT under docker's data-root. Docker here reports DockerRootDir=/mnt/data/docker AND driver-type io.containerd.snapshotter.v1 — with the containerd image store, images live under containerd's own root, which has no override. So `/` grows with every image pull while /mnt/data stays nearly empty: measured 2026-08-28, **`/` 79% used** (21 GB containerd + 7.6 GB stale /var/lib/docker) against **/mnt/data at 11%**.

`/var/lib/docker` is the pre-migration leftover. It is dead weight on the fuller of the two filesystems — and it is what the old cache collector was measuring.
